title: I'm building a real-time clothing design and simulation tool for the web
author: obraiadev
selftext:
I've recently been working on another project where I wanted to have more realistic cloth and hair simulations. I couldn't find many good solutions that could run efficiently in the browser, so I decided to try building my own.

That eventually led me to the need for a way to create the clothes themselves, so I'm now working on this application, which will allow users to design, simulate, and export garments.

I'm currently developing and testing everything on a Mac mini M4.

https://reddit.com/link/1y5bkne/video/0f3hhw6j6s3i1/player

Aqui estou tentando fazer a jaqueta de couro do Jensen Huang:

https://reddit.com/link/1y5bkne/video/6muukvcv8s3i1/player

I'll also need a way to create physics-based hair for my other project, so I'm planning to build a separate tool for that in the future as well.

Just for context, the project is inspired by tools like Marvelous Designer and CLO3D.

comments.author: obraiadev
comments.body: Yes, I am using XPBD with particle-based collision.

comments.author: obraiadev
comments.body:
https://i.redd.it/i13d9sarjs3i1.png

All the clothes are designed in 2D as patterns and seams. Then, when you start the simulation, they come together around the character and, if everything is set up correctly, they end up looking like actual clothes.

comments.author: obraiadev
comments.body: This isn't something I came up with, a few well-known tools already work this way. As for the zipper: the slider and pull are still fairly basic models made from a few simple shapes. I plan to replace them later, maybe even let users upload their own. The pull hangs from the slider on a hinge with physics enabled, so it swings when things move. The teeth are generated in code along both edges of the seam marked as a zipper. The solver is what drives the cloth: it pulls the two sides together up to the slider and lets them spread apart past it, which gives the zipper its V-shaped opening.
